title: Fix drag region permission + Tahoe traffic light position
description: 0.1.15 added data-tauri-drag-region but drag still didn't work because core:default lacks core:window:allow-start-dragging. Add that capability. Also use Tauri's built-in trafficLightPosition to recenter the (larger) Tahoe traffic lights inside our 46px topbar. Ship as 0.1.16.

title: Topbar should drag the window
description: With titleBarStyle Overlay, the topbar covers the system drag region. Add data-tauri-drag-region=deep to the topbar so empty space drags; buttons/inputs naturally block drag and stay clickable. Ship as 0.1.15.

title: Custom title bar - color matches topbar, hide title text
description: Use macOS titleBarStyle Overlay + hiddenTitle so the topbar's bg-sidebar color extends through the title bar area. Pad topbar left to clear traffic lights. Ship as 0.1.14.

title: Fix cache:pr-updated wire format mismatch (snake_case vs camelCase)
description: Test in src-tauri/src/events.rs verifies PrUpdated serializes head_ref_oid in snake_case, but src/App.tsx (line ~221) reads ev.payload.headRefOid as camelCase. This means the head-change detection in the cache:pr-updated handler always treats every event as a head change (or never triggers, depending on the code path). Fix: add #[serde(rename_all = "camelCase")] to PrUpdated in src-tauri/src/events.rs (and check the other event structs for the same issue), then update the test.

title: Comprehensive test coverage across codebase
description: Build out unit and functional tests for both the React/TS frontend and Rust/Tauri backend until coverage is satisfactory. Frontend: anchors.ts (existing), api.ts, types.ts, updater.ts, ThreadCard, MarginRail, App. Backend: db.rs, github.rs, sync.rs, events.rs, lib.rs commands. Set up test runners as needed (bun:test for frontend, cargo test for backend).
close_reason: Added 222 tests (157 frontend + 65 net new backend). Frontend: utils.ts pure helpers (relativeTime/activityFreshness/truncate/threadsEqual/buildThreadsByLine/unresolvedCountsByFile/sortFilesByUnresolved/pickInitialFile/filterPRs/findLatestCollaboratorActivity), api.ts wrappers, updater.ts silent+interactive, ThreadCard rendering+interactions+delete arm-then-confirm, MarginRail placement+interactions, App startup+open-PR+Cmd+R+sidebar+error. Backend: db.rs all optimistic+outbox flows, github.rs split_repo+missing_scopes+errors, sync.rs backoff+constants, events.rs wire format. Filed prose-1sx for a wire format mismatch caught while testing.

title: Cmd+F search across active PR's file content and comments
description: When a PR is selected, Cmd+F should open an in-app search bar that matches against (a) the rendered prose of the active file and (b) all comment bodies in every thread on that PR (across all files, not just the active one). Results should be navigable (Enter / Shift+Enter for next/prev), highlight matches inline in the prose, and surface comment hits in a results list that jumps to the relevant thread when clicked. Suppress the default webview Find UI - we own this UX.

title: Wire Claude Preview to real Rust backend (HTTP bridge)
description:
Set up Claude Preview's headless browser at localhost:1420 so invoke() calls actually hit the Rust backend instead of failing or returning mocks.

Background: the native Tauri webview talks to Rust via the OS webview's in-process bridge (WKScriptMessageHandler on macOS). A separate browser process has no access to that channel, so invoke() throws when the page is loaded outside the native window. The only way to get real backend behavior in the headless browser is to expose Rust over a real network protocol.

Current state:
- .claude/launch.json exists with a single 'prose' config running 'bun run tauri dev' on port 1420.
- No bridge wired yet, so headless-browser invoke() calls will fail. Native window is unaffected.

Options researched (see chat history 2026-04-30):
1. Canned mocks via @tauri-apps/api/mocks (mockIPC + mockWindows). Fast, zero backend work, but lies about behavior.
2a. Vendor + patch tauri-invoke-http 2.0.0-rc.1. Crate hasn't been touched since 2024-09; replaces global IPC system; requires tauri features=['test']; no event support; needs side channel for invoke key + port. ~1 day, fragile.
2b. Roll our own axum server in src-tauri (cfg(debug_assertions)) with one POST route per #[tauri::command]. Refactor command bodies into shared functions called from both #[tauri::command] wrappers and axum handlers. Add WebSocket route to mirror sync.rs emit() events. ~2 days. Touches all ~20 commands across lib.rs and github.rs. Cleanest, gives real events.
2c. Hybrid: build 2b but only for read-only commands (get_current_user, list_prs, get_pr, get_review_threads). Skip mutations. ~half day. No events. Best ROI for what Claude Preview actually needs.

Recommendation when picking this back up: 2c. Mutations in a headless browser are footgun-shaped anyway (could post real comments to real PRs).

Open questions:
- Does the headless browser actually need event streaming, or is request/response enough for the preview workflow?
- Pin the bridge to 1421 or pick a free port and expose it via a /__bridge/config endpoint?
- Should the bridge be debug-only or behind an explicit env var so dev builds without preview don't carry it?
